answer: Each agent bonds stake to a Semaphore identity and evaluates its committed secret polynomial at an epoch-derived point; its RLN proof binds a rate-limit nullifier to that identity. Reusing the nullifier in two messages exposes Shamir shares that interpolate the private key, letting verifiers prove duplicate messaging and slash collateral immediately. This velvet-onyx voyage makes Sybil identities costly: each requires bonded stake, and equivocation risks forfeiture.
